context:
Goal: the phone app's Tally rows look like the web's.
Problem: on the phone, a long set name in a Tally row's second line is cut off with no "…". The web shows "…". The phone can too, but then Apple's accessibility check flags the line as cut-off text. Skipping that check needs your word, as with items 19 and 29.
Based on: the web's Tally row ends a long line in "…" (read, src/app.jsx:1345).
Based on: VoiceOver reads the whole line either way (assumed, not checked).
Meanwhile: Restyle pushed step 4's other review fixes. Step 4's look check waits for the simulator.
holds: Step 4's last review failed on this, so step 4 can't merge until it's settled.

options.gain: Matches the web, and you can see the name is cut.
options.how: The line ends in "…". Apple's cut-off-text check is skipped on this one line only.
options.label: Show "…", as the web does
options.lose: One more named skip in the checks.

options.gain: No skip, and nothing is hidden.
options.how: A long line wraps instead of being cut.
options.label: Wrap to two lines
options.lose: Long rows get taller, unlike the web.

options.how: The text is cut off with no "…".
options.label: Keep the hard cut
options.lose: Text is cut with no cue, and it doesn't match the web.

ref: step 4 polish review round 1; web src/app.jsx:1345; decision card-tally-row-counts-first
title: A long set name in a Tally row: show "…" like the web?
why: It's what the web already does. VoiceOver should still read the full name, but nobody has checked that yet.
